sections.html:
Jefferson Parish is home to Kenner, the biggest incorporated suburb of New Orleans. Its 66,448 residents in 2020 made it Louisiana's sixth largest city. It covers about 15 square miles, bounded by Lake Pontchartrain to the north and the Mississippi to the south. Metairie and River Ridge lie to the east and St. Charles Parish to the west, so a Kenner house is rarely far from a levee, a drainage canal or a pumping station.

Most of the housing north of Airline Highway did not exist before the late 1950s. Swamp was drained and filled, and Interstate 10 plus road improvements in the 1960s pushed the suburb outward fast. Population climbed from 5,535 in 1950 to 66,382 by 1980. Many Kenner houses are mid-century builds on filled ground, so shoppers in the northern subdivisions raise drainage and settling. Older streets sit closer to the river around Rivertown, founded in 1855 by Minor Kenner. Getting around means Interstate 10, U.S. 61 (Airline Drive) or Louisiana 49 (Williams Boulevard).

Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport sits inside the Kenner city limits, just south of Interstate 10. It brings aircraft noise to some blocks and a steady stream of travelers and airport workers who need housing nearby.

Noise is nothing to hide. Because the state form asks what you know about the house, a straight answer about overhead aircraft protects you.

  • Ask a neighbor or two how often planes pass over at different times of day.
  • Keep any insulation or window upgrades you did and mention them.
  • Frequent flyers will like how close the terminal is.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Kenner house?
sections.html:
Kenner owners get two tax bills: parish taxes are collected by the Jefferson Parish Sheriff, and the City of Kenner bills its share separately. Value comes from the assessor, though the assessor has no say over the rate. The assessor's number is 504-362-4100.

Tax ruleJefferson Parish detail
Residential assessment ratio10% of fair market value
Homestead exemptionFirst $7,500 of assessed value, equal to $75,000 of market value, on an owner-occupied home
Kenner 2025 combined millage0.10625 (parish 0.07809, city 0.02816)
ReappraisalAt least every four years; the last full one was 2016

Kenner is ward 92. The combined millage works out to about 106 mills. The city portion is figured without subtracting the homestead exemption, so it applies to the full assessed value.

Your exemption is canceled once you sell or move, and a Louisiana home can carry only one. The new owner must go to the assessor's office in person, bringing a recorded copy of the act of sale and a photo ID with the property address. That recorded act is the paper they need. Seniors and some disabled owners can hold a frozen assessed value, but it belongs to the owner and does not transfer to a buyer.

sections.h2: Tax calendar and selling in the fall
sections.html: The parish roll is filed by November 15, and payment is due by December 31. From the next day, a balance is delinquent and gains one percent interest monthly (R.S. 47:2127). Selling in autumn? Have the closing notary explain who pays this year's bill, so you are not still liable for a house that is no longer yours.

sections.h2: How is a house sale made legal in Louisiana?
sections.html:
Louisiana lets land or a house change hands by authentic act or by act under private signature. Under Article 1839 of the Civil Code, outsiders are bound only after the paper is filed for registry in the parish of the property. For Kenner that means Jefferson Parish: the act is signed, then recorded with the clerk, and only then is the buyer protected against third parties.

  • Sign the act of sale at closing, normally in front of a notary.
  • The Jefferson Parish clerk then files it for registry.
  • The buyer later brings a recorded copy to the assessor for homestead.
  • A remaining mortgage is paid off from proceeds and cancelled of record.

R.S. 9:3198 makes a residential seller fill out a property disclosure form and hand it over by the moment the buyer makes an offer. A buyer who receives it late can cancel or withdraw within 72 hours, with weekends and holidays excluded, and gets deposits back. The form is no warranty, and a seller who passes on a public body's or professional's report in good faith is not liable for errors in it. Where you lack knowledge, the form allows you to say so.

Buyers in Kenner care most about water, wind and noise. Note any past flood claims, roof replacements and drainage work. Hurricane Katrina in 2005 brought widespread East Bank flooding in Jefferson Parish, especially in Metairie and Kenner, so buyers will ask.

sections.h2: What city rules apply if a Kenner house is empty or in poor shape?
sections.html:
Kenner keeps an abandoned property registry under Ordinance 10455, and its Inspection and Code Enforcement Department takes permits and complaints. Each vacant property needs an annual registration form. An inherited house left empty may be on that list already, and one that draws complaints can pile up fines, so check.

The code department is at 1926 18th Street, Kenner, LA 70062, and the permits desk is at 504-468-4062. Ask about unfinished permits so a buyer hears what remains open.

Selling as-is can end the exposure. Registration, repairs and permit work pass to a cash buyer, and your open projects stay unfinished.

sections.h2: Steps from offer to closing in Kenner
sections.html:
Once an offer is accepted, a notary starts the title search and your lender provides a payoff. Pull together the deed, tax bill, flood and roof records and permit papers. Financed buyers add an appraisal and inspection. Cash buyers can close when title work is clear. At signing, the loan balance, unpaid taxes and recording fees are deducted from your proceeds. Request the settlement statement in advance and question any charge.

Choose your route based on condition and schedule. A listing reaches the most buyers but depends on financing, an appraisal and showings. A cash sale is usually faster and may skip repairs, though the offer tends to come in lower than a polished listing. For a Kenner house with drainage trouble, an open code file or an inherited title, a cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands can remove several steps at once. Before you agree to any offer, work out your net after the payoff, taxes and closing costs so you can compare choices on equal terms. Keep copies of everything you sign.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a house in Kenner?
faqs.a: Parish tax is collected by the Jefferson Parish Sheriff, while the City of Kenner sends a second bill. The assessor sets the value and has no control over the rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kenner house that has an open code complaint?
faqs.a: Yes, in its current condition, but tell the buyer about the complaint. The Kenner Inspection and Code Enforcement Department can say what is open and whether the house is registered as abandoned.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. It ends when you sell or move out. The buyer must apply in person at the assessor's office with the recorded act of sale and photo ID.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a disclosure form in Louisiana?
faqs.a: Yes. Deliver it by the time the buyer makes an offer. If it comes later, the buyer has 72 hours to back out.

faqs.q: Does airport noise change what I have to say?
faqs.a: Mention it if it affects the house, because the form asks what you know. Saying so plainly is safer than leaving it out.
